Recursion is a methodical problem-solving technique where a function solves a complex task by breaking it down and calling upon a smaller, identical version of itself. Imagine an archivist organizing a massive library by dividing it into smaller sections, then recursively organizing each section until they reach individual, easily cataloged books. To prevent an infinite loop of endless division, the process must include a clearly defined base case that stops the self-referencing once the smallest unit is reached. Finally, the solutions from these smallest units are systematically passed back up the chain, combining to resolve the original, larger task.
